cases.sentence: Нынче идет ___, почти мокрый, желтый и мутный.
cases.translation: Today the snow is falling, almost wet, yellow, and murky.
cases.explain: «Снег» is the subject of the verb «идёт» (snow is falling), taking the nominative case.

cases.sentence: Разве можно человека без ___ на 40 лет одного оставлять?
cases.translation: Is it possible to leave a person alone without occupation for 40 years?
cases.explain: The preposition «без» always governs the genitive case: «без дела» = 'without occupation.'

cases.sentence: Я там 40 лет сряду к этим вашим ___ в щелочку прислушивался.
cases.translation: For 40 years straight I listened in through the crack to these words of yours.
cases.explain: The preposition «к» governs the dative case: «к словам» = 'to these words.'

cases.sentence: Кроме того, может быть, я от записывания действительно получу ___.
cases.translation: Besides, perhaps I will really get some relief from writing.
cases.explain: «Облегчение» is the direct object of «получу» (I will receive), requiring the accusative case.

cases.sentence: ...до сих пор всегда обходил их, даже с каким-то ___.
cases.translation: ...he had always avoided them until now, even with a certain unease.
cases.explain: The preposition «с» governs the instrumental case: «с беспокойством» = 'with unease.'

cases.sentence: ...и в то же время в нашем ___ заискиваете.
cases.translation: ...and at the same time you curry favor in our opinion.
cases.explain: The preposition «в» governs the prepositional case: «в мнении» = 'in our opinion.'

reading.ru: Я хоть и сказал, что завидую нормальному человеку до последней желчи, но на таких условиях, в каких я вижу его, не хочу им быть.
reading.question: What does the narrator say about the "normal man"?
options: He envies him bitterly but doesn't want to be him under the conditions he sees
He wants to become him immediately
He has never thought about him
reading.correct: He envies him bitterly but doesn't want to be him under the conditions he sees
reading.explain: He says he envies the normal man 'to the last drop of bile' but doesn't want to be him on those terms.

reading.ru: Вру, потому что сам знаю, как дважды два, что вовсе не подполье лучше, а что-то другое, совсем другое, которого я жажду, но которого никак не найду.
reading.question: What does the narrator admit he is really longing for?
options: Something else entirely, which he craves but can never find
reading.correct: Something else entirely, which he craves but can never find
reading.explain: He admits he is lying, because he knows it isn't the underground that's better, but 'something else, quite different,' which he craves but can't find.

reading.ru: А вот посадил бы я вас лет на сорок безо всякого занятия, да и пришел бы к вам через сорок лет в подполье.
reading.question: What hypothetical scenario does the narrator propose for "you" (his readers)?
options: Being left forty years with nothing to do, then visited in the underground
Being given all the money in the world
Being sent to school for forty years
Being made king for forty years
reading.correct: Being left forty years with nothing to do, then visited in the underground
reading.explain: He imagines placing his reader idle for forty years, then visiting them in the underground after that time.

reading.ru: Разве можно человека без дела на 40 лет одного оставлять?
reading.question: What rhetorical question does the narrator ask about leaving a person idle?
options: Whether it's possible to leave a person alone with nothing to do for 40 years
Whether 40 years is too short a punishment
Whether 40 years old is too young to work
reading.correct: Whether it's possible to leave a person alone with nothing to do for 40 years
reading.explain: He asks, 'Is it possible to leave a person alone without occupation for 40 years?'

reading.ru: Вы жаждете жизни и сами разрешаете жизненные вопросы логической путаницей.
reading.question: What does the narrator accuse "you" of doing with life's questions?
options: Resolving them with logical confusion, while craving life itself
reading.correct: Resolving them with logical confusion, while craving life itself
reading.explain: He says 'you thirst for life, yet you resolve life's questions with logical confusion.'

reading.ru: Вы из самого мелкого часа вынесете правду на показ, на позор, на рынок.
reading.question: According to the narrator, what will "you" do with the truth, even from the smallest moment?
options: Put it on display, on show, on the market, for shame
reading.correct: Put it on display, on show, on the market, for shame
reading.explain: He accuses 'you' of dragging out the truth 'on display, to shame, to market' from even the smallest hour.

reading.ru: Разумеется, все эти ваши слова я сам теперь сочинил.
reading.question: What does the narrator admit about the accusing words he attributed to "you"?
options: He made them all up himself
They were quoted from a real reader's letter
They were printed in a newspaper
reading.correct: He made them all up himself
reading.explain: He confesses, 'Of course, I made up all these words of yours myself.'

reading.ru: Есть в воспоминаниях всякого человека такие вещи, которые он открывает не всем, а разве только друзьям.
reading.question: What does the narrator say exists in every person's memories?
options: Things one reveals only to friends, not everyone
reading.correct: Things one reveals only to friends, not everyone
reading.explain: He says there are things in everyone's memories that one reveals only to friends, not to all.

reading.ru: И таких вещей всякого порядочного человека довольно-таки накопится.
reading.question: What does the narrator claim accumulates in any decent person, and increases the more decent he is?
options: Things even he is afraid to reveal to himself
reading.correct: Things even he is afraid to reveal to himself
reading.explain: He says such hidden things accumulate in every decent person, and the more decent he is, the more there are.

reading.ru: Замечу, кстати, Гейна утверждает, что верная автобиография почти невозможна, и человек сам обо себе не думает.
reading.question: What does the narrator say Heine (Гейне) claims about autobiography?
options: That a truthful autobiography is almost impossible
That autobiography is the highest literary form
reading.correct: That a truthful autobiography is almost impossible
reading.explain: He notes Heine asserts that a truthful autobiography is almost impossible, since a man is bound to lie about himself.

reading.ru: Я очень хорошо понимаю, как иногда можно единственное из одного тщеславия наклепать на себя целое преступление.
reading.question: What does the narrator say vanity alone can make a person do?
options: Falsely confess to an entire crime out of vanity alone
reading.correct: Falsely confess to an entire crime out of vanity alone
reading.explain: He says he understands how one can, out of sheer vanity, slander himself with an entire invented crime.

reading.ru: Ну вот, например, могли бы придраться к слову и спросить меня, если вы действительно не рассчитываете на читателей, то для чего же вы теперь делаете с самим собой еще на бумаге такие уговоры, то есть что порядком из системы заводить не будете, что запишите то, что припомнится и так далее, и так далее.
reading.question: What objection does the narrator imagine readers raising, if he claims not to be writing for an audience?
options: Why does he still make such agreements with himself on paper, as if writing for someone
Why does he refuse to name names
Why is his handwriting so messy
reading.correct: Why does he still make such agreements with himself on paper, as if writing for someone
reading.explain: He imagines being asked why, if he doesn't count on readers, he still makes such arrangements with himself on paper.

reading.ru: Вот нынче, например, меня особенно давит одно давнишнее воспоминание.
reading.question: What is weighing on the narrator "today," as he begins to write?
reading.explain: He says one long-standing memory in particular is weighing on him today.

reading.ru: Говорят, от работы человек добрым и честным делается.
reading.question: What do people say happens to a person through work, according to the narrator?
reading.explain: He notes, 'They say a man becomes kind and honest through work.'

reading.ru: Итак, пусть это будет повесть по поводу мокрого снега.
reading.question: What does the narrator decide to call the tale he is about to tell?
options: A tale apropos of the wet snow
reading.correct: A tale apropos of the wet snow
reading.explain: He concludes, 'So let this be a tale apropos of the wet snow.'
